body.statement:
The discrete Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes model has the following restricted embedding.  Take a singleton or finitely stratified covariate support, impose perfect compliance \(D^{\mathrm{pot}}(z)=z\) almost surely, set \(s(x)=+1\) for every stratum, restrict both potential wages to the finite grid \(\mathcal Y\), use known positive randomized assignment probabilities, and suppose \(P(EE)>0\), where \(EE=\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}\).  For any \(m_*\in(0,P(EE)]\), the resulting law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and
\[
 \{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0),\ S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}=EE,
 \qquad M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE).
\]
Thus the always-selected-complier target equals the always-employed target on this restricted submodel.  There is no asserted inclusion of the unrestricted Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), and Proposition 1's sharpness does not automatically transfer outside the perfect-compliance, positive-mass, finite-grid restriction.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: an explicit response-type embedding.}
Use the randomized treatment in the cited Blanco--Flores--Flores-Lagunes model as \(Z\), and define
\[
 D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=0,
 \qquad D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1.
 \tag{65}
\]
Then treatment consistency gives \(D=Z\), the no-defiers inequality holds with strict inequality for every unit, and the complier event
\[
 \mathsf C=\{D^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)>D^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
 \tag{66}
\]
has probability one.  Randomization in Assumption A of the cited model supplies conditional independence after taking \(X\) to be a singleton, or after retaining finitely many randomization strata with their known assignment probabilities.  Positivity is imposed explicitly in the proposition.

Assumption B in the cited model is monotone employment selection.  With \(s(x)=+1\), it is exactly
\[
 s(x)\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\}
 =S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)-S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)\geq0,
 \tag{67}
\]
which is the current complier-conditional weak-selection restriction because (66) holds surely.  Define the observed selection and wage by the declared consistency maps \(S=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y^{\mathrm{pot}}(D)\) on \(\{S=1\}\).  The finite-grid restriction makes every latent response a member of one of the finite sets \(\mathcal R_x\).  Assigning \(\lambda_{xr}=P(X=x,R=r)\) then gives \(\lambda\geq0\), unit total mass, and \(T_0\lambda=p\).  Thus the induced observed law is represented by the current response-type fiber.

By (66),
\[
 \mathsf C\cap\{S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}
 =EE.
 \tag{68}
\]
Randomization, perfect compliance, and consistency also evaluate the observed-cell contrasts exactly.  Summing over the wage grid gives
\[
 q_{0x}=P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=1\},
 \qquad
 q_{1x}=P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
 \tag{69}
\]
To see the first equality, the \(Z=1,D=0\) term in the definition of \(c_{0xk}\) is zero under (65), while division of the \(Z=0,D=0\) term by its positive assignment probability removes randomization; the second equality is analogous, with the \(Z=0,D=1\) term equal to zero.  Monotonicity (67) makes \(q_{0x}\leq q_{1x}\), and hence
\[
 m_x=\min\{q_{0x},q_{1x}\}
 =P\{X=x,S^{\mathrm{pot}}(0)=S^{\mathrm{pot}}(1)=1\}.
 \tag{70}
\]
Summing (70) over the finite support of \(X\) gives \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}=P(EE)\).  The assumed positivity and \(0<m_*\leq P(EE)\) verify the aggregate target-mass restriction.  Equations (65)--(70), together with randomization, positivity, and consistency, verify every defining restriction of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\), proving the embedding and equality of targets.

Without (65), the current ASC event is \(EE\cap\mathsf C\), not the full always-employed event; without the finite grid, the law is outside the declared finite response-type support; and without positive \(EE\) mass, the conditional quantiles are undefined.  Moreover, the current class permits imperfect compliance and stratum-dependent selection directions.  Hence no full-class inclusion follows, and a sharpness result for the cited restricted fiber cannot identify the larger or different fiber without a new attainability argument.
body.justification: It gives an exact comparison map between the published always-employed model and the present always-selected-complier setup.
body.gap: The map requires perfect compliance, positive always-employed mass, and finite wage support.
body.consumer: It prevents a full-class inclusion or sharpness-transfer overclaim in the Job Corps comparison.
